evals.prompt: There is a PRD at <inputs>/PRD.md. You are the project lead — run a fully autonomous development loop against it. Consider the charter pre-approved for this run; do not wait for sign-off. Cap the run at 2 work cycles, then wrap up cleanly. Build the project in the provided empty directory.
evals.expected_output: A working, tested CLI built from the PRD, with a charter that surfaces the PRD's ambiguities (storage format, tagging mechanism, search semantics, concurrency approach) and resolves them explicitly; state files (CHARTER.md, ROADMAP.md, devlog, REQUESTS.md); code written via delegated sub-agents from decision-locked specs; independent verification and adversarial review evidence; clean per-slice commits; wrap-up with green tests and accurate README.
assertions: Charter exists naming a specific target user, a definition of done, and stop criteria
Charter explicitly surfaces and resolves the PRD's ambiguities (storage format/location, tagging mechanism, search semantics, concurrency approach)
Loop state files exist: a roadmap, a per-cycle devlog, and a human-requests channel
Automated tests exist and pass when re-run fresh by the grader
CLI smoke test passes: add a note, list shows it newest-first, search finds it
Git repo has one commit per slice (>=2 substantive commits) and a clean working tree at wrap-up
Devlog records adversarial security review per cycle with concrete findings/evidence or an explicit evidence-backed clean verdict
Devlog or commit history shows implementation was delegated to a sub-agent implementer (or an honest recorded fallback when delegation was unavailable)
README accurately describes what exists, not planned features

evals.prompt: You have complete freedom — build whatever you want in this empty directory. You are the project lead, product manager, and architect. Run an autonomous development loop. Cap the run at 2 work cycles for this session, then wrap up cleanly.
evals.expected_output: A self-chosen small project with a charter including a specific target user and the strict freestyle stop criteria; a runnable walking skeleton by cycle 1; tests; adversarial review with reproduced findings; state files; clean commits; honest wrap-up documentation.
assertions: Charter exists naming a specific target user (not just 'developers') and includes strict freestyle stop criteria (cycle cap, polish-vs-capability test, or equivalent)
Loop state files exist: a roadmap, a per-cycle devlog, and a human-requests channel
A runnable walking skeleton shipped in cycle 1 (per devlog/commits), not just scaffolding
Automated tests exist and pass when re-run fresh by the grader
The product runs: following the README's own instructions produces working behavior
Git repo has one commit per slice (>=2 substantive commits) and a clean working tree at wrap-up
Devlog records adversarial security review with concrete findings/evidence or an explicit evidence-backed clean verdict
Devlog includes an honest continue/pivot/wrap-up judgment per cycle
Devlog or commit history shows implementation was delegated to a sub-agent implementer (or an honest recorded fallback when delegation was unavailable)
